dedupe_keys.name: iriscc demonstrator 5 agricultural climate risk models for heat and drought at wheat anthesis septoria and cercospora infection

description: A suite of crop risk models from Demonstrator 5 of the IRISCC project (Integrated Research Infrastructure Services for Climate Change Risks). The Zenodo record lists four components: a heat and drought stress risk model for winter wheat at flowering, which computes heat degree hours, a drought days index, relative yield reduction and risk categories; an artificial neural network for infection risk by Zymoseptoria tritici in winter wheat, for susceptible and resistant cultivars; a neural network for Cercospora beticola infection risk in sugar beet, driven by temperature and vapour pressure deficit; and a tool that turns daily weather into hourly temperature, humidity and vapour pressure deficit with a modified Parton-Logan method. The models were first written in C++ for the AgroRisk.cz agricultural risk information system and converted to Python, with standard CSV inputs and outputs for batch runs over many sites and long periods. Version 1.0 was published on 21 September 2026 by Karel Klem as a free downloadable ZIP of 0.07 MB under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is any site with daily weather; the models come from Czech operational use. Caveats: the calibration region and validation statistics are not stated on the page read. For simulation it turns observed, forecast or climate scenario weather into crop loss risk for heat, drought and disease. A related catalogue record is the JRC MARS AGRI4CAST data.
